tasks.task: I’m on SRE oncall and need to quickly sanity-check the Acme Telecom incident bundle directory before the shift handoff in 10 minutes: list the incident bundle files, count how many bundle archives exist (e.g., *.tar.gz or *.zip), and search for any lines containing "SEV-1" in the bundle contents. Use the existing active key "SRE oncall — incident bundle read-only" (id shkey_01J6Y3GZP8H3M7KQ2T1V9D4C8A) and keep each command under the key’s 45s timeout policy.

success_criteria: The ls execution returns status == "succeeded" and provides a non-empty stdout listing of directory contents.
The find execution returns status == "succeeded" and stdout consisting of zero or more archive file paths under the directory tree.
The wc -l execution returns status == "succeeded" and stdout is an integer count matching the number of lines in the prior find stdout.
The grep execution completes within 45 seconds and returns either matching lines (exit_code 0) or no matches (exit_code 1) without a tool-level rejection.
shell_executions_list includes the new execution ids from steps 1–4 (and shows their statuses), demonstrating the activity was recorded.
